questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of this molecule?

q_image.alt: Bond-line structure: a chain of four carbons with a one-carbon branch on the second carbon

choices.why: Same chain, numbered from the wrong end. Number from the end nearer the branch, so the methyl gets locant 2, not 3.
Right. The longest chain has 4 carbons (butane), and numbering from the end nearer the branch puts the methyl on C2.
Drawn as named, this is the same molecule, but the chain chosen is too short: the longest chain has four carbons, not three, so the parent is butane and the name is 2-methylbutane.

image.alt: Bond-line structure drawn as the name 2-ethylpropane says: a three-carbon chain with a two-carbon (ethyl) branch on the middle carbon

choices.why: Drawn as named, this is the same molecule, but the chain chosen is too short. The ethyl group extends the longest chain to 4 carbons, so the parent is butane.

steps: Find the longest continuous carbon chain: 4 carbons, so the parent is butane.
The one branch is a CH₃ group: a methyl substituent.
Number the chain from the end nearer the branch: the methyl is on C2.
Put the locant and prefix before the parent name: 2-methylbutane.

steps: Find the longest chain: BrCH₂–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH₃ has 4 carbons, so the parent is butane.
The substituents are Br (bromo) and CH₃ (methyl). Halogens are named as prefixes, like alkyl groups.
Number for the lowest locants: from the Br end they are 1 and 3; from the other end, 2 and 4. So Br is on C1 and the methyl on C3.
List the prefixes in alphabetical order (bromo before methyl): 1-bromo-3-methylbutane.

answer_image.alt: Bond-line structure of 2,3-dimethylpentane: a five-carbon zigzag with a methyl branch on the second and on the third carbon

steps: Parent pentane: draw a zigzag of 5 carbons. Each corner and each line end is one carbon.

questions.q: How many neutrons are in the ion ³⁷Cl⁻?

choices.why: Right. Chlorine has Z = 17, so N = A − Z = 37 − 17 = 20. The 1− charge changes the number of electrons, not the number of neutrons.
17 is Z, the number of protons. The number of neutrons is A − Z.
18 is the number of electrons in Cl⁻ (17 + 1). The charge changes only the electrons.
37 is the mass number A: protons and neutrons together. Subtract Z = 17 to get the neutrons.

steps: Chlorine is element 17, so Z = 17 (17 protons).
The superscript is the mass number: A = 37.
Neutrons: N = A − Z = 37 − 17 = 20.
The 1− charge means one extra electron (18 electrons) and does not change the nucleus.

questions.q: Draw the Lewis structure of carbonic acid, H₂CO₃, in your notebook. Show every lone pair and give the formal charge of each atom.

answer_image.alt: Lewis structure of carbonic acid, H₂CO₃: a central carbon with one C=O and two C–O–H groups, two lone pairs on every oxygen, and all formal charges 0.

steps: Count valence electrons: 2 H + C + 3 O = 2 + 4 + 18 = 24.
Skeleton: C in the center bonded to three O atoms, with one H on each of two O atoms. These 5 single bonds use 10 electrons, leaving 14.
Give each OH oxygen 2 lone pairs and the O without H 3 lone pairs: 4 + 4 + 6 = 14 electrons, all used.
C has only 3 bonds, so move one lone pair of the O without H into a C=O double bond. Every atom now has a full shell.
Formal charges: C = 4 − 0 − ½ × 8 = 0, each O = 6 − 4 − ½ × 4 = 0, each H = 1 − 0 − ½ × 2 = 0. All formal charges are 0.

questions.q: What is the hybridization of each carbon in ClCH₂C≡CH, from the CH₂ carbon to the carbon at the end?

q_image.alt: Lewis structure of 3-chloroprop-1-yne, ClCH₂C≡CH: chlorine with three lone pairs bonded to a CH₂ carbon, then a carbon–carbon triple bond ending in C–H. All formal charges are 0.

choices.why: Right. The CH₂ carbon has 4 electron groups (Cl, two H and C), so it is sp³. Each alkyne carbon has 2 electron groups, because the triple bond counts once, so both are sp.
The triple bond counts as one electron group, so each alkyne carbon has 2 groups, not 3. Two groups → sp. sp² fits a carbon in a C=C double bond.
The CH₂ carbon has four single bonds (4 electron groups) and no π bond, so it is sp³, not sp².
Only a carbon with 2 electron groups (two π bonds) is sp. The CH₂ carbon has 4 groups, so it is sp³.

steps: CH₂ carbon: bonded to Cl, two H and the next C, no lone pairs: 4 electron groups → sp³.
Middle carbon: bonded to the CH₂ carbon and the end carbon. The triple bond counts once, so 2 electron groups → sp.
End carbon: bonded to the middle carbon and one H: 2 electron groups → sp.
Check with π bonds: each alkyne carbon has 2 π bonds (sp), and the CH₂ carbon has none (sp³). The H atoms are not hybridized.

questions.q: What is the molecular shape around the oxygen of the hydronium ion, H₃O⁺?

q_image.alt: Lewis structure of the hydronium ion, H₃O⁺: oxygen with three O–H bonds and one lone pair, and a formal charge of +1 on oxygen.

choices.why: Right. O has 4 electron groups (3 H and 1 lone pair), so the parent geometry is tetrahedral. The lone pair is not counted in the shape, so O and the three H atoms form a pyramid.
Tetrahedral is the parent geometry of the 4 electron groups. The molecular shape names only atoms, and one corner holds a lone pair.
Trigonal planar needs 3 electron groups and no lone pair, as in BF₃. The O in H₃O⁺ has a fourth group, its lone pair, which pushes the H atoms out of one plane.
Bent means 2 bonded atoms, as in H₂O. H₃O⁺ has 3 H atoms bonded to O.

steps: Count the electron groups on O: 3 bonded H atoms and 1 lone pair, 4 groups.
4 groups → parent geometry tetrahedral (O is sp³).
Name the shape from the atoms only: O with 3 H atoms and the lone pair on the fourth corner is trigonal pyramidal.
The H atoms are not hybridized.

picture_check.note: O-T0a v3 drawing by Chem Sketcher, approved by Yishi 2026-11-23.

questions.q: In CO₂, which two orbitals overlap head-on to form the σ bond of each C=O?

q_image.alt: Lewis structure of carbon dioxide: O=C=O with two double bonds, two lone pairs on each oxygen, and a formal charge of 0 on every atom.

choices.why: Right. C has 2 electron groups, so it is sp. Each O has 3 electron groups (C and two lone pairs), so it is sp². The σ bond is the head-on overlap of these two hybrid orbitals.
The carbon of CO₂ has only 2 electron groups (the two O atoms), so it is sp, not sp².
Side-on overlap of two unhybridized 2p orbitals forms the π bond of C=O, not the σ bond.
sp³ needs 4 electron groups. In CO₂ the carbon has 2 and each O has 3.

steps: Carbon: 2 electron groups (the two O atoms, no lone pairs) → sp.
Each oxygen: 3 electron groups (the C atom and two lone pairs) → sp².
σ bond: a carbon sp hybrid overlaps head-on with an oxygen sp² hybrid, along the C–O axis.
π bond: an unhybridized 2p orbital on C overlaps side-on with the parallel 2p orbital on O. Carbon's second 2p orbital makes the π bond to the other O.

questions.q: In your notebook, draw H₂CO₃ and label every atom except H with its hybridization and the shape around it. For each kind of oxygen, also name the parent geometry its shape is derived from.
questions.answer: C sp² · O= sp² · OH sp³

answer_image.alt: H₂CO₃ labeled with hybridization and shape: carbon sp² and trigonal planar, the C=O oxygen sp² and linear, derived from trigonal planar, the OH oxygens sp³ and bent, derived from tetrahedral. The hydrogens carry no hybridization label.

steps: C: 3 electron groups (three O, no lone pairs) → sp², trigonal planar, 120°.
C=O oxygen: 3 electron groups (C and two lone pairs) → sp², parent trigonal planar. Only one bonded atom, so its geometry is linear.
Each OH oxygen: 4 electron groups (C, H and two lone pairs) → sp³, parent tetrahedral. Two bonded atoms, so its shape is bent.
Lone pairs count as electron groups for the hybridization and the parent geometry, but not in the name of the shape.
The H atoms get no label: hydrogen is not hybridized.

questions.q: Which of these molecules has a dipole moment of zero (μ = 0)?

choices.why: Right. Each B–F bond is polar, but the three equal bond dipoles point 120° apart in one plane (trigonal planar), so they cancel.
NH₃ is trigonal pyramidal. The three N–H dipoles all tilt toward N and add, together with the lone pair, so μ is not zero.
H₂O is bent. Both O–H dipoles point toward O and do not cancel, so μ is not zero.
Both Br atoms are on the same side of the C=C, so the two C→Br dipoles add toward the bromines. The trans isomer is the one with μ = 0.

steps: Find the polar bonds: B–F, N–H, O–H and C–Br are all polar, so polarity depends on the shape.
BF₃ is trigonal planar: three equal dipoles 120° apart cancel, μ = 0.
NH₃ (trigonal pyramidal) and H₂O (bent): the dipoles point toward the central atom and add.
cis-1,2-dibromoethene: both C→Br dipoles point to the same side and add. Only BF₃ has μ = 0.

questions.q: Draw each compound in your notebook and write its molecular formula: A oxetane, B cyclobutanol, C allyl alcohol (prop-2-en-1-ol), D cyclopropylmethanol, E cyclopropanol. Then group the ones that are constitutional isomers of each other.
questions.answer: A, C, E: C₃H₆O · B, D: C₄H₈O

answer_image.alt: Five structures with their molecular formulas: A oxetane C₃H₆O, B cyclobutanol C₄H₈O, C allyl alcohol C₃H₆O, D cyclopropylmethanol C₄H₈O, E cyclopropanol C₃H₆O.

steps: A, oxetane: a four-membered ring of 3 C and 1 O. Each ring carbon has 2 H, so 6 H. Formula C₃H₆O.
B, cyclobutanol: a four-carbon ring with OH on one carbon. 3 CH₂ (6 H) + 1 CH (1 H) + the OH hydrogen = 8 H. Formula C₄H₈O.
C, allyl alcohol, CH₂=CH–CH₂–OH: 3 C and 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 6 H. Formula C₃H₆O.
D, cyclopropylmethanol: a three-carbon ring with a CH₂OH group. Ring 2 + 2 + 1 = 5 H, CH₂ 2 H, OH 1 H, 8 H in all. Formula C₄H₈O.
E, cyclopropanol: a three-carbon ring with OH on one carbon. 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 6 H. Formula C₃H₆O.
Check with the 2n + 2 rule: each compound has one ring or one C=C, so H = 2n + 2 − 2 = 2n: 6 H for 3 C and 8 H for 4 C.

Same formula, different connectivity: A, C and E are constitutional isomers of each other (C₃H₆O), and so are B and D (C₄H₈O). A compound from one group is not an isomer of one from the other, because the formulas differ.

picture_check.note: O-T0a v3 drawing by Chem Sketcher, approved by Yishi 2026-11-23.

choices.why: Right. Both are C₂H₆O. In ethanol the O is bonded to C and H (C–O–H), and in dimethyl ether to two C atoms (C–O–C): same formula, different connectivity.
The formulas differ: butane is C₄H₁₀ and 2-methylbutane is C₅H₁₂. Isomers must have the same formula.
Same formula and the same connectivity, BrCH=CHBr. They differ only in their arrangement in space, so they are stereoisomers, not constitutional isomers.
The formulas differ: propane is C₃H₈ and propene is C₃H₆.

steps: Write each formula first: ethanol C₂H₆O and dimethyl ether C₂H₆O. butane C₄H₁₀ and 2-methylbutane C₅H₁₂. propane C₃H₈ and propene C₃H₆. Both dibromoethenes are C₂H₂Br₂.
Keep only the pairs with the same formula: ethanol with dimethyl ether, and the two dibromoethenes.
Compare connectivity: ethanol is C–C–O–H and dimethyl ether is C–O–C, so the bonding differs.
The cis and trans dibromoethenes are both Br–C=C–Br with the same bonds: stereoisomers.
Constitutional isomers: ethanol and dimethyl ether.

questions.q: Which of these solvents is polar aprotic?

choices.why: Right. Acetone has a polar C=O bond (a large dipole) but no O–H or N–H, so it cannot donate hydrogen bonds.
Methanol has an O–H bond, so it donates hydrogen bonds: it is polar protic.
Water has two O–H bonds: it is polar protic.
Hexane has only C–C and C–H bonds: it is nonpolar, with dispersion forces only.

steps: Polar protic solvents have an O–H or N–H bond and donate hydrogen bonds: water and methanol.
Nonpolar solvents have only C–C and C–H bonds: hexane.
Polar aprotic solvents are polar but have no O–H or N–H: acetone, with its polar C=O and every H on carbon.
Answer: acetone is polar aprotic.
